claims.quote: The voice of another aerocab driver hailing them made them realize that there were still ties that bound them to Earth
claims.description: Passenger aircraft-cabs fly through the air and dock with one another in mid-flight.

claims.quote: Ralph had immediately transmitted the lost girl's photograph to the Central Office where it was placed before a Telephot connecting with every member of the entire police force
claims.description: A device sends images to police officers across the city in real time through a single central screen.

claims.quote: and the picture was reproduced for them in their portable radio instruments for ten seconds, enabling them to get her features firmly impressed on their minds.
claims.description: Portable radio receivers display transmitted pictures on the spot for officers.

claims.quote: Towards the end of the twenty-first century, when atmospheric flying had become common, scientists began seriously to think of constructing machinery to enable man to leave the confines of the planet to which humanity had been chained for ages.
claims.description: Machines able to carry people out of the atmosphere into space are imagined once flight within air is common.
claims.stated_time: Towards the end of the twenty-first century

claims.quote: although that body was known to have no atmosphere and was known to be sterile, it was equally well known that Earth's scientists and engineers felt that they could, in a few years' time, make it habitable.
claims.description: Engineers are believed able to make the airless moon habitable for people within a few years.

claims.quote: This scientist had made extensive studies of the gyroscope and had finally evolved a machine which when set in motion would rise freely and continue to rise as long as power was supplied.
claims.description: A gyroscope-based device is imagined that lifts itself off the ground and keeps rising while powered, an anti-gravity machine.

claims.quote: Space flyers were equipped with from six to twelve large anti-gravitators attached to various points of their shells, all of which could be worked in unison, or operated independently in order to control the direction of the flyer.
claims.description: Spacecraft carry several anti-gravity units placed around their hulls to steer and lift them.

claims.quote: Inside of a space flyer, which had an infinitely small gravity, objects weighed practically nothing.
claims.description: Objects inside a spacecraft far from planets become weightless.

claims.quote: Dozing off is all he can do, and that could never last long, except after strenuous mental work.
claims.description: Crew in space cannot sleep properly because there is nothing to tire them out.

claims.quote: The air supply was manufactured by chemical means on board, but very little was needed, as the original supply taken from the earth is used over and over by altering the carbonic acid gas by means of automatic generators.
claims.description: A spacecraft recycles its air with automatic chemical generators that convert exhaled carbon dioxide.

claims.quote: Thus between every two celestial bodies a point will be found where the attraction that one body exerts on the other is zero.
claims.description: A point exists between any two celestial bodies where their gravitational pulls cancel out.

claims.quote: it would begin to turn around on its own axis, while at the same time moving in an elliptical orbit around the sun
claims.description: A craft left at a balance point between two bodies would become a small free-orbiting planet.

claims.quote: On the sun, however, he would weigh 2232 kilograms.
claims.description: A person's weight on the sun is stated as about 2,232 kilograms for a body that weighs 80 kilograms on Earth.

claims.quote: Surely, not to Venus where the inhabitants were nearly all Terrestrials, and whose laws were identical with those of Earth.
claims.description: Venus is imagined as a settled world whose people are mostly Earth-born and governed by Earth's laws.

claims.quote: From the intensity and the elapsed time of the reflected impulses, the distance between the earth and the flyer can then be accurately and quickly calculated.
claims.description: Radar-like polarized waves reflected off a craft let its distance from Earth be calculated.

claims.quote: but it was not until the year 2659 that […] succeeded in accurately determining the exact location of flyers, in space, beyond the reach of the most powerful telescope.
claims.description: Craft far out in space are located precisely by an instrument, which is first achieved in the year 2659.
